text: Bid the tricks you can count, not the ones you hope for.
Unsure between two bids? Take the lower one. A bag hurts less than a set.
Aces are near-sure tricks. Kings need company in their suit to count.
Long spades are gold: every trump past your third often wins a late trick.
A short side suit is a trumping chance. Add a little to your bid for it.
Your bid plus your partner's is one contract. Think team total.
Partner bid big? You may only need to chip in a trick or two.
Count the jokers and deuces as they fall so you know which trumps are left.
Track each suit: once a suit has gone around twice, expect someone to trump it.
The Big Joker is the boss. Know where it is before you lead a high trump.
Never trump a trick your partner is already winning.
Don't fight your partner for tricks they've already got covered.
Go Nil only with low cards in every suit and few, small spades.
A lone king or queen in a short suit is a Nil trap. It has nowhere to hide.
Holding a joker or the 2 of spades? That's a trump trick. Skip the Nil.
Nil works best when your partner has a strong hand to protect you.
Partner bid Nil? Win the tricks they can't safely duck, even cheap ones.
Covering a Nil: lead your aces early so your partner can dump danger cards.
Covering a Nil: save your top trumps for the end, when your partner is most exposed.
Against a Nil, lead low cards and make the Nil bidder take something.
Made your bid? Start ducking. Play the highest card that still loses.
Bags add up fast and cost you big, so keep an eye on the count.
Opponents loaded with bags? Feed them cheap tricks they can't refuse.
Setting a big bid is worth more than dodging a bag or two.
Opponents bid high? Hold your top trumps to steal their key tricks.
Lead from your strong side suits early, before others run short and trump.
Don't burn high trumps on cheap early tricks. Save them for aces.
Once spades are broken, leading high trumps can pull the opponents' last trumps.
Late in the hand, count what's left. Your low trump may now be a winner.
Behind late in the game? A well-timed Nil can swing the score fast.
